new_statements.quote: All Sedang words have a stressed main syllable (fonique) (e.g. pui « shin ») ; many words also have an unstressed presyllable (prefonique) (topui « to talk »). [...] Ro-, ho-, ros-, hos-, s-, and rs- are a group of presyllable variants which occur before voiceless stops p, t, and k [...] « hand span »). S- is the presyllable of Kotua Sedang on the east. [p.196, résumé:] Tous les mots sédangs ont une syllable tonique (e.g. pui « tibia ») ; il y a aussi beaucoup de mots qui ont une syllable prétonique (e.g. topui « parler »). [...] s- est la syllabe prétonique du dialecte sédang des kotua à l'est.
new_statements.translation: (French part) All Sedang words have a tonic [stressed] syllable (e.g. pui 'shin'); there are also many words that have a pretonic syllable (e.g. topui 'to speak'). ... s- is the pretonic syllable of the Sedang dialect of the Kotua in the east.

new_statements.relation_note: Group-level statement for all the Sedang dialects surveyed (which explicitly include Kotua Sedang of Mang Buk): every word has a stressed main syllable, optionally preceded by an unstressed presyllable; s- is named as the (unstressed) presyllable characteristic of Kotua Sedang. Vowel register treated as part of the word; no tone.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Words consist of an obligatorily stressed main syllable, optionally preceded by one unstressed presyllable (sesquisyllabic/iambic), i.e. stress on the final (main) syllable; asserted for all Sedang dialects in the survey, Kotua Sedang of Mang Buk included.
new_statements.exceptions: none; presyllables may be dropped, metathesized or vary by area (ro-/ho-/s-/ros-/rs-/hos-)
new_statements.identity_note: Smith 1967 describes 'MangBuk Kotua (Kotua Sedang)', spoken 'in the Mang Buk area, about 30 kilometers east-northeast of Toumorong', as the eastern border dialect of Sedang (p.204) and includes it among the Sedang dialects covered by his 178-item checklist. Katua [kta] is located at Mang Buk (Măng Bút, Kon Plông; Glottolog 14.90N 108.29E), but Smith 1973 (MKS 4: 113-118, fn. 2) later reports that only 2 of the c. 22 villages resettled at Mang Buk are Kotua, the rest Sedang, and that Kotua proper (his Feb. 1969 list) is a separate East North Bahnaric language without register. So the 1967 'Kotua Sedang' informants may have spoken Sedang (seda1262) of the Mang Buk area rather than Katua; unresolved. [name in source: Kotua Sedang (KtSed); MangBuk Kotua; 'le sédang des kotua'; pages 196 (French résumé), 200, 204, 208 (informant list: 79 = Kotua Sedang, Mang Buk, 3 informants), 210]

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2009. How many branches in a tree? Cua and East (North) Bahnaric. In Bethwyn Evans (ed.), Discovering history through language: papers in honour of Malcolm Ross, 193-204. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 605.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Section 3 'Cua and Kơtua' (pp. 196-199) re-uses Smith's 1973 Kơtua forms in Tables 3-4 (nasal hardening, vowel restructuring) and concludes Kơtua 'is found here to be solidly North Bahnaric' (p. 193); fn. 7 notes Diffloth & Zide 1992 relegate Kơtua to 'uncertain' status. No independent Kơtua data and no phonological description.
sources.venue: Discovering history through language: papers in honour of Malcolm Ross

sources.citation: Smith, Kenneth D. 1973. Eastern North Bahnaric: Cua and Kơtua. Mon-Khmer Studies 4: 113-118.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. The only published Kotua data: c. 40 forms from a 200-word list taken at Mang Buk in Feb. 1969 (informant Nai of Thu Thok village, fn. 4, p. 117). Comparative-historical notes only: final-nasal hardening after non-nasal/non-laryngeal initials, no vowel-register contrast (p. 114), loss of final r, final l > w, voiced fricative z, affricate ts, voiceless lateral fricative hl, prenasalized voiced stops, sometimes prestopped final nasals (p. 116). Disyllabic forms with presyllables occur in the data (apau 'mortar', kaneng 'crossbow', katsek 'bone') but no word-structure or stre…

sources.citation: Smith, Kenneth D. (compiler). 1970. Vietnam word list (revised): Kơtua. Manuscript, 5 pp., dated 20 Feb 1970 (informant Nai of Thu Thok village, 2 days' walk E of Mang Buk; 'Dialect: kotua = ko'nan Sedang'). SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 35772 (draft posted 2009). [= Glottolog ref 309453 'Vietnam Word List: Kotua', the languoid's Glottolog's most extensive description]
sources.note: No phonology content: a bare 281-prompt SIL 'Vietnam word list (revised)' form with c. 200 Kotua responses in an unkeyed practical roman orthography (the 'Key to orthography' line holds the informant's name instead). No statement on stress, accent or tone anywhere; no stress or tone marks (only a few breve/grave vowel diacritics and one apostrophe in ko'neh 'fall'). Word shapes visible: monosyllables and sesquisyllables with presyllables kơ-/ko-/to-/a- (kơtăp 'egg', kotsèk 'bone', tokoăng 'bark', apau 'mortar', koneng 'crossbow'), prenasalised onsets (mbreq 'sand', nggrul 'river', njek 'leg')…
